question.text: A hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ is charged with a charge $Q .$ The electric potential and intensity inside the sphere are respectively

solution.text: Inside a hollow charged sphere, the electric field intensity is always zero. $\therefore$ $E=0$ but potential is constant. Potential on the surtace of the hollow sphere $$ V=\frac{K Q}{R}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}} \cdot \frac{Q}{R}=\frac{Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R} $$ This is the potential $(\mathrm{V})$ inside the charged hollow meta sphere.
